title.en: Streets Paved with Golden Pebbles: The Coronation Wedding of Huayna Capac
title.zh: 街道鋪滿金礫:瓦伊納·卡帕克的加冕婚禮

source.work: Juan de Santa Cruz Pachacuti-yamqui Salcamayhua, 'An Account of the Antiquities of Peru', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: After the fall of Hualpaya the councillors ruled three years, then prepared the coronation feast, assigning to Huayna Ccapac as wife his own sister Ccoya Mama Cusirimay, according to the custom of his ancestors. They were married on the day of the coronation: all the walls and roofs of the city were covered with rich plumes, and the streets were paved with golden pebbles. The Ynca came forth from the house of his grandfather Pachacuti followed by the Apu Curacas of Colla-suyu; Mama Cusirimay came from the palace of Tupac Ynca Yupanqui attended by the Curacas of the other suyus. The Ynca and his spouse entered the temple of the Creator Pachayachachi, each by a separate door, shod in llanques of gold. Raised to the platform, he said a prayer in a loud voice which concluded the day's proceedings and they were considered married. After three days the tupac-yauri and suntur-paucar were delivered, then the ccapac-llautu and unincha, the ccapac-unancha or royal standard, and the huaman-champi of two edges. The Ynca took an oath and touched the ground, promising to emulate the deeds of his forefathers, to attend to the things of Pachayachachi and his Ccuricancha, and to do no evil to the kingdom; then the Apu Challca Yupanqui said a prayer to the Creator, beseeching him to guard and protect the Ynca with his powerful hand.
summary.zh: 瓦爾帕亞伏誅後,眾臣執政三年,籌備加冕大典,依祖先舊俗,以王姊科亞·瑪瑪·庫西里瑪伊為瓦伊納·卡帕克之妻。加冕之日成婚:全城牆垣屋頂遍覆華羽,街道鋪以金礫。印加王自祖父帕查庫提之宅而出,科利亞蘇尤諸庫拉卡扈從;王后自圖帕克·尤潘琪之宮而出,餘三蘇尤庫拉卡侍從。王與后各由一門入造物主帕查亞查奇之神廟,足登金鞋。登台之後,王高聲誦禱,禱畢即視為成婚。三日後授圖帕克-亞烏里權杖與孫圖爾-保卡爾,再授卡帕克-勞圖頭帶、烏寧恰、卡帕克軍旗與雙刃瓦曼戰斧。王宣誓並以手觸地,誓效祖先功業、敬奉帕查亞查奇與其科里坎查、毋害大蘇尤之邦。大祭司阿普·查爾卡·尤潘琪隨之向造物主祈禱,求其以大能之手護佑印加王。

sensitivity.note: Coronation liturgy from the native-authored chronicle; sibling marriage recorded as dynastic custom.

passages.text: After three years they began to prepare for the feast of the coronation; and they assigned as the wife of Huayna Ccapac his own sister Ccoya Mama Cusirimay, according to the custom of his ancestors. They were married on the day of the coronation, when all the walls and roofs in the city were covered with rich plumes of feathers, and the streets were paved with golden pebbles. The people were gorgeously dressed in cumpis and plumes. They say that fifty thousand men guarded the city and the fortress of Sacsahuaman, and that the festival was a wonderful sight.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Salcamayhua, Antiquities of Peru (Markham 1873); not verbatim.

passages.text: The Ynca and his spouse then entered the temple, each by a separate door, the temple being that of the Creator Pachayachachi; the High Priest was called Apu Challcu Yupanqui. The sovereign and his wife were shod in llanques of gold; and afterwards they gave him the chipana of gold and raised him to the platform whence he performed these ceremonies, where he said a prayer in a loud voice, which concluded the proceedings of that day, and they were considered to be married. Afterwards they delivered to him the tupac-yauri and the suntur-paucar, after three days, and the ccapac-llautu and the unincha in the same place where they were married.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Salcamayhua, Antiquities of Peru (Markham 1873); not verbatim.

passages.text: The Ynca took an oath and touched the ground, promising to emulate the deeds of his forefathers, and to attend to the things of Pachayachachi and his Ccuricancha, and to do no evil to the kingdom of Ttahuantin-suyu, keeping the laws of former Yncas, and favouring all loyal servants. Then the Apu Challca Yupanqui said a prayer to the Creator, beseeching him to guard and protect the Ynca with his powerful hand, and to defend him from his enemies. Those present then shouted out their acclamations, and all praised the Creator called Pachayachachi Uiracochan. Then the Ynca went to the Huacay-pata, where was his ccapac-usnu, and there each chief and captain, in his order, promised obedience to the new sovereign.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Salcamayhua, Antiquities of Peru (Markham 1873); not verbatim.

texts.canonical_translation: C. R. Markham, Narrative of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas (Hakluyt Society, 1873)

title.en: The Sister Who Refused: Signs of Blood in the Heavens

source.work: Juan de Santa Cruz Pachacuti-yamqui Salcamayhua, 'An Account of the Antiquities of Peru', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: Huayna Ccapac wished to marry his second sister, named Mama Cuca, who refused her consent; he then ill-treated her and began to use force, but her prayers and menaces made him desist. Then he went with presents and offerings to the body of his father, praying him to give her for his wife; but the dead body gave no answer, while fearful signs appeared in the heavens, portending blood. This was called Ccalla-sana. It made Huayna Ccapac give up his intention in regard to his sister, so he gave her to a very old and ugly Curaca who was a great chewer of coca - not for her good, but in order to bring shame upon her. She wept; and leaving the old man, whose name was Hacaroca, she entered the house of the Acllas as a princess, and became abbess, never having submitted to the old man. The Ynca was then married a second time, but not with such ceremonies, to Ccoya Chimpu Runtucay.
summary.zh: 瓦伊納·卡帕克欲娶次妹瑪瑪·庫卡,妹不允;王遂相逼,幾欲用強,然其妹哭求與怒斥並至,王乃罷手。王攜禮物祭品至先王遺體前,求亡父將此妹賜己為妻;亡父無言,而天際卻現可怖之兆,預示流血——此謂「卡利亞-薩納」。王遂打消娶妹之念,將她許給一位極老極醜、嗜嚼古柯的庫拉卡——非為其好,實欲羞辱之。妹泣;離開老翁哈卡羅卡,以公主之身入阿克亞貞女之屋,後為女院長,始終未屈身老翁。王乃第二次成婚,禮數較簡,娶科亞·欽普·倫圖卡伊。

sensitivity.note: The rejected-sister episode with its heaven omens; the mummy-consultation motif recurs in this cycle.

Then he went with presents and offerings to the body of his father, praying him to give her for his wife, but the dead body gave no answer, while fearful signs appeared in the heavens, portending blood. This was called Ccalla-sana.

title.en: The Oracle of Pachacamac Speaks Alone to the Inca
title.zh: 帕查卡馬克神諭獨對印加王

region.en: Ccuricancha of Pachacamac, coast of Lima (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 帕查卡馬克科里坎查(今利馬海岸)(象徵性標記)

source.work: Juan de Santa Cruz Pachacuti-yamqui Salcamayhua, 'An Account of the Antiquities of Peru', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: In those days messengers came from Rimac bringing word that, within the Ccuricancha of Pachacamac, the huaca had said that it desired to see the Ynca. So he went to visit Pachamac, and the huaca spoke to him alone, saying that he must take riches to Chimu, and honour it more than Uiracochan Pachayachachi. The Ynca consented, and the wizards rejoiced. But the Ynca was to blame, Salcamayhua says, for having confided in the promises of the huaca at Pachacamac and other idols: in the following war his Colla-suyu army was destroyed and his men left starved and in rags, while the war became more fierce than ever.
summary.zh: 彼時里馬克遣使來報:帕查卡馬克的科里坎查內,瓦卡有言,欲見印加王。王遂往訪帕查卡馬克,瓦卡獨對王而言:命他攜重寶至奇穆,並敬奉此瓦卡超越維拉科查·帕查亞查奇。王允之,眾巫歡騰。然而薩爾卡馬瓦說,王之過,在於輕信帕查卡馬克瓦卡與諸偶像的許諾:其後戰爭中,科利亞蘇尤大軍盡歿,部眾飢寒交迫,戰事反愈演愈烈。

sensitivity.note: The Pachacamac oracle episode linking coastal cult and highland kingship; the author's moralizing frame preserved.

passages.text: In those days messengers came from Rimac, bringing word that, within the Ccuricancha of Pachacamac (the Ccuricancha was a temple, and there were many in different parts, the largest being in Cuzco), the huaca had said that it desired to see the Ynca. So he went to visit Pachamac, and the huaca spoke to him alone, saying that he must take riches to Chimu, and honour him more than Uiracochan Pachayachachi. The Ynca consented, and the wizards rejoiced. But the Ynca was to blame for having confided in the promises of the huaca at Pachacamac and other idols. His men were now left starved and in rags, while the war became more fierce than ever.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Salcamayhua, Antiquities of Peru (Markham 1873); not verbatim.

texts.canonical_translation: C. R. Markham, Narrative of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas (Hakluyt Society, 1873)

title.zh: 亞瓦爾-科查:被血染紅的湖

region.en: Lake Yahuar-ccocha, near Otabalo, Ecuador (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 奧塔瓦洛附近亞瓦爾-科查湖(今厄瓜多)(象徵性標記)

source.work: Juan de Santa Cruz Pachacuti-yamqui Salcamayhua, 'An Account of the Antiquities of Peru', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: In the war against the Cayambis the Colla-suyu troops, ordered to take the enemy in the rear, marched very leisurely; the Cayambis fell upon them furiously and caused great slaughter, so that few escaped of the fine and powerful army of Colla-suyu. Reinforced at last, the Ynca attacked in three columns; the Colla-suyus climbed the fortresses of the Cayambis and attacked them fiercely, sparing neither age nor sex, the Ynca fighting in person. The Cayambis fled to the montañas of Otabala and assembled on the shores of a lake, where they were surrounded and there was great slaughter. The warriors washed their arms in the lake, and there was a mass of blood in the centre, so the lake was called Yahuar-ccocha - the lake of blood.
summary.zh: 征卡揚比之役,奉命迂迴敵後的科利亞蘇尤軍行動遲緩,被卡揚比人猛撲,屠戮殆盡。援軍既至,印加王分三路進攻:科利亞軍攀上卡揚比人的山寨,猛烈衝殺,老幼婦孺不留;印加王親自督戰。卡揚比人退往奧塔瓦洛山間,聚於一湖之濱,遭四面合圍,殺戮極慘。戰士們在湖中洗滌武器,湖心盡是血污,故名此湖為「亞瓦爾-科查」——血湖。

sensitivity.note: Battle-name etiology; the lake-name is still on the map near Otavalo.

passages.text: The Colla-suyu troops had been ordered to take the enemy in the rear, but meanwhile the Cayambis did great injury to the royal camp, and discovered that the Colla-suyus were marching very leisurely. So they fell upon them furiously, and caused great slaughter, so that few escaped in the fine and powerful army of Colla-suyu.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Salcamayhua, Antiquities of Peru (Markham 1873); not verbatim.

title.en: The Box of Butterflies: The Message That Killed Huayna Capac
title.zh: 蝴蝶之盒:致瓦伊納·卡帕克於死的信使

source.work: Juan de Santa Cruz Pachacuti-yamqui Salcamayhua, 'An Account of the Antiquities of Peru', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: The Ynca advanced beyond Pasto but returned to Quito, where he solemnized the Ccapac-Raymi. At the hour for eating a messenger arrived in a black mantle, who reverently kissed the Ynca and gave him a pputi covered up. The Ynca told the messenger to open it, but he excused himself, saying that the command of the Creator was that the Ynca alone should do so. So the Ynca opened it, and there came flying out a quantity of things like butterflies or bits of paper, which spread abroad until they disappeared. This was the pestilence of sarampion, and in a few days the general Mihicnaca Mayta died, with many other captains, their faces being covered with scabs. When the Ynca saw this, he ordered a house to be built of stone, in which he hid himself, and there died. After eight days they took out the body quite dried up, and embalmed it, and took it to Cuzco on a litter, richly dressed and armed as if it had been alive. A son, named Tupac Atahualpa, was left in Quito with many chiefs and captains - Quis-quis, Challcuchima, Unacchuyllu, Rumi-ñaui, Ucumari, and many more.
summary.zh: 印加王遠征至帕斯托之外,折返基多,隆重舉行卡帕克-雷米祭。進餐時分,一名身披黑氅的信使來到,恭敬吻王之手,獻上一只覆蓋的「普普提」(小盒)。王命信使開盒;信使推辭,說造物主之命:唯印加王可開。王親啟之——盒中飛出無數似蝴蝶、似紙屑之物,四散飛揚,直至消失。此即「薩拉姆皮翁」(麻疹?)瘟疫。數日之間,大將米克納卡·馬伊塔與眾多隊長相繼死去,面上滿布痂痕。王見狀,命人以石築屋,自匿其中,竟死於斯。八日後啟視,遺體已乾,乃敷香裹殮,以轎抬回庫斯科,衣甲鮮明,一如生前。基多留有王子圖帕克·阿塔瓦爾帕,與基斯-基斯、查爾庫奇馬、烏納丘尤盧、魯米-尼亞維、烏庫馬里等大將。

sensitivity.note: The smallpox epidemic narrated as a boxed plague of butterflies sent by the Creator - one of the most striking omens in Andean literature.

title.en: Married to the Dead: How Huascar Made His Mother Legitimate
title.zh: 與亡者成婚:瓦伊斯卡爾之「正名」

source.work: Juan de Santa Cruz Pachacuti-yamqui Salcamayhua, 'An Account of the Antiquities of Peru', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: The body of Huayna Ccapac was conveyed to Cuzco with much ceremony and deposited with the other bodies of the Yncas; there was general mourning. Then Yuti Tupac Cusi Huallpa Huascar Ynca made his mother, Rava Ocllo, marry the dead body, in order that he might become legitimate, and the ministers of the temple performed the ceremony out of fear. Thus Tupac Cusi Huallpa took the title of legitimate son of Huayna Ccapac, and called upon all the chiefs of Ttahuantin-suyu to swear obedience to him, which was done. He induced the great Curacas to ask the ministers of Ccuricancha to deliver to him the ccapac-llautu, suntur-paucar, tupac-yauri and ccapac-uncu; at the end of a year he received the ccapac-llautu with the name of Yuti Cusi Huallpa Huascar Ynca. He married his sisters Chuqui-huy-pachuquipa and Ccoya Mama Chuqui huypa chuquipa.
summary.zh: 瓦伊納·卡帕克的遺體以大禮運回庫斯科,與歷代印加遺體同殿安放,全國舉哀。尤蒂·圖帕克·庫西·瓦爾帕(瓦伊斯卡爾)為使自己的嫡子身份成立,竟令其母拉瓦·奧克略與亡父遺體「成婚」;神廟執事懼其威,遂行婚儀。圖帕克·庫西·瓦爾帕自此稱瓦伊納·卡帕克之嫡子,召大蘇尤眾酋宣誓效忠,眾皆從之。他並促使眾庫拉卡請科里坎查執事授予卡帕克-勞圖、孫圖爾-保卡爾、圖帕克-亞烏里與卡帕克-溫庫。一年後,他受卡帕克-勞圖,稱「尤蒂·庫西·瓦爾帕·瓦伊斯卡爾·印加」,並娶其妹楚基-瓦伊-帕丘基帕與科亞·瑪瑪·楚基-瓦伊-帕丘基帕。

sensitivity.note: The mummy-marriage: legitimacy manufactured through the ancestor cult; a uniquely Andean political rite.

passages.text: The body of Huayna Ccapac was conveyed to Cuzco with much ceremony, and the people made obeisances to it. After it was deposited with the other bodies of the Yncas, there was general mourning for his death. Then Yuti Tupac Cusi Huallpa Huascar Ynca made his mother, Rava Ocllo, marry the dead body, in order that he might become legitimate, and the ministers of the temple performed the ceremony out of fear.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Salcamayhua, Antiquities of Peru (Markham 1873); not verbatim.

passages.text: Thus Tupac Cusi Huallpa took the title of legitimate son of Huayna Ccapac, and called upon all the chiefs of Ttahuantin-suyu to swear obedience to him, which was done. He then prepared for his coronation, and induced the great Curacas to ask the ministers of Ccuricancha to deliver to him the ccapac-llautu, suntur-paucar, tupac-yauri, and ccapac-uncu. Great preparations were made for the coronation, and there was a distribution of rich dresses, plumes, and arms. At the end of a year he received the ccapac-llautu, with the name of Yuti Cusi Huallpa Huascar Ynca.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Salcamayhua, Antiquities of Peru (Markham 1873); not verbatim.

texts.canonical_translation: C. R. Markham, Narrative of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas (Hakluyt Society, 1873)

title.en: The Damsels Cried to Heaven: Huascar's Outrage at Pocana-cancha
title.zh: 貞女仰天呼號:瓦伊斯卡爾在波卡納-坎恰的暴行

region.zh: 維爾卡斯地區波卡納-坎恰(象徵性標記)

source.work: Juan de Santa Cruz Pachacuti-yamqui Salcamayhua, 'An Account of the Antiquities of Peru', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: On his return to Cuzco, passing through Titicaca where he set up a golden image of the sun, Huascar came to Pocana-cancha, where he found all the Apu Curacas coming in their litters according to the privilege granted by former Yncas. In this place he ordered the Acllas, of all four classes, to be brought into the open square, in the middle of all the Apu Curacas and the whole army. Then he told a hundred Indians of the Llama-llamas and Hayacuchos, while they were performing their dances, to seize the damsels and ravish them in public. The damsels, when they were thus treated, cried out and raised their eyes to heaven; and all the great men of the kingdom resented such conduct, and looked upon this Huascar Ynca as half a fool, and only treated him with reverence from fear.
summary.zh: 瓦伊斯卡爾回師庫斯科,途經的的喀喀,立太陽金像而拜,稱之為「維拉科查·因蒂」。行至波卡納-坎恰,見歷代印加特許乘轎的眾庫拉卡相繼而至。在此地,他命將四個等級的阿克亞貞女全部帶到大廣場中央——眾庫拉卡與全軍眼前——並命一百名利亞馬-利亞馬斯與哈亞庫科斯人趁起舞之際,當眾擄掠、姦污這些女子。貞女受辱,仰天哭號;王國的顯貴們無不憤恨,皆視瓦伊斯卡爾為「半個瘋子」,只因畏懼才表面恭敬。

sensitivity.note: The outrage on the Aclla houses' wards is recorded here as a dynastic indictment, part of the moral case against Huascar in the civil-war cycle.

passages.text: On his return to Cuzco he came to Pocana-cancha, where he found all the Apu Curacas coming in their litters according to the privilege granted by former Yncas, and Huascar Ynca laughed at this, although he did not take away the privilege. In this place he ordered the Acllas, of all four classes, to be brought into the open square, in the middle of all the Apu Curacas and the whole army. Then he told a hundred Indians of the Llama-llamas and Hayacuchos, while they were performing their dances, to seize the damsels and ravish them in public.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Salcamayhua, Antiquities of Peru (Markham 1873); not verbatim.

passages.text: The damsels, when they were thus treated, cried out and raised their eyes to heaven; and all the great men of the kingdom resented such conduct, and looked upon this Huascar Ynca as half a fool, and only treated him with reverence from fear.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Salcamayhua, Antiquities of Peru (Markham 1873); not verbatim.

title.en: Drums of the Messengers' Skins: The Insult That Started the War
title.zh: 信使之皮製鼓:引爆內戰之辱

region.zh: 基多與庫斯科(象徵性標記)

source.work: Juan de Santa Cruz Pachacuti-yamqui Salcamayhua, 'An Account of the Antiquities of Peru', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: At that time Tupac Atahuallpa sent to Huascar Ynca, beseeching him to give him the title and nomination of Governor of the Provinces of Quito, and the Ynca Huascar granted the request, and gave him the name of Ynca-ranti. Then the chief of the Cañaris, named Urco-calla, brought false news to Huascar Ynca, asking him why he consented that Tupac Atahuallpa should have the title of Ynca. This enraged the Ynca, and when Tupac Atahuallpa sent him rich presents he caused them to be burnt, and drums to be made of the skins of the messengers who brought them, except a few, whom he sent back to Quito dressed as women, and with very shameful messages to Auqui Atahuallpa. They were followed by a chief named Huaminca-atoc, whom the Ynca sent against Atahuallpa with 1200 men, and orders to take him and the other captains prisoners. The surviving messengers arrived at Quito and reported what had happened to Auqui Tupac Atahuallpa, who received the news in great sorrow, but in silence. The captain replied he would answer by his deeds; and Auqui Atahuallpa, with the consent of all his captains, determined to take up arms: the people of Quito swore to obey him, he assumed the title of Ynca, began to use a litter, and assembled 13,000 warriors.
summary.zh: 其時,圖帕克·阿塔瓦爾帕遣使求瓦伊斯卡爾封他為基多諸省總督;瓦伊斯卡爾允其所請,賜名「印加-蘭蒂」。然而卡尼亞里人酋長烏爾科-卡利亞向王進讒,問王為何容許阿塔瓦爾帕僭用印加之號。王大怒:阿塔瓦爾帕獻上的重禮被他付之一炬,並剝來使之人皮製鼓;僅留數人,男扮女裝,攜極盡羞辱之語送回基多。王又遣將瓦明卡-阿托克率一千二百人往執阿塔瓦爾帕及其諸將。生還的信使抵基多報信,阿塔瓦爾帕聞之,大慟而默然。他遣人問瓦明卡-阿托克興師何為,對方答曰「以行動作答」。阿塔瓦爾帕遂得眾將之諾,決意起兵:基多民眾宣誓效忠,他僭稱印加之號,乘坐轎輦,聚兵一萬三千。

sensitivity.note: The insult-cycle opening the civil war; the skin-drums motif is one of the war's signature atrocities.

title.en: The Two Lumps of Grease: The Oracle of the Burning Camps
title.zh: 兩塊油脂:燃燒營地的神諭

region.en: Hill of Cocha-cassa, near Cuzco (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 庫斯科附近科查-卡薩山(象徵性標記)

source.work: Juan de Santa Cruz Pachacuti-yamqui Salcamayhua, 'An Account of the Antiquities of Peru', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: At midnight Challcuchima and Quisquis lighted a fire on their left hands with a piece of grease; putting one lump of grease to represent the camp of Huascar Ynca, and the other for the camp of Atahuallpa. And the one in the place of Huascar Ynca burnt much more than that in the place of Atahuallpa, so that the grease of Huascar, burning up so high, went out very quickly, while that of Atahuallpa went on burning. Then Challcuchima and Quisquis sang the haylli, and told their men that all would go well. They set out for Utcu-pampa in search of Huascar Ynca, and got there at sunset with six hundred and forty men, when the Ynca was asleep, and took him prisoner, routing the Rucanas who were his bearers, and so they carried him to Sallcantay. When the army found that Huascar Ynca was taken they were terrified, and each tribe went off to its own land.
summary.zh: 午夜,查爾庫奇馬與基斯-基斯以一塊油脂在左手邊生火:一塊脂代表瓦伊斯卡爾之營,一塊代表阿塔瓦爾帕之營。代表瓦伊斯卡爾的那塊油燒得猛烈異常,火苗高竄,轉瞬即熄;而代表阿塔瓦爾帕的那塊油卻持續燃燒不熄。二將遂唱「阿伊利」凱歌,告訴部眾:大事必成。他們率六百四十人於日落時抵烏特庫-潘帕,趁瓦伊斯卡爾酣睡之際將其生擒,擊潰其轎伕魯卡納斯人,押往薩爾坎泰。大軍聞王被擒,駭然四散,各族各歸故土。

sensitivity.note: Fire-grease divination before the decisive capture; a Quechua oracle rite recorded by a native author.

title.en: Chillca Leaves Instead of Coca: The Outraged Huascar Cries to the Creator
title.zh: 以奇爾卡葉代古柯:受辱的瓦伊斯卡爾哭訴造物主

region.zh: 庫斯科附近凱帕伊-潘帕(象徵性標記)

source.work: Juan de Santa Cruz Pachacuti-yamqui Salcamayhua, 'An Account of the Antiquities of Peru', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: They insulted the Ynca by tying a rope round his neck, and Quisquis called him Cocahacho and Sulluya, which means bastard, eater of coca, and offered him many other affronts. Then Quisquis and Challcuchima abused the mother of the Ynca, saying: 'Come here, Mama Ocllo, you who were the concubine of Huayna Ccapac.' When Huascar heard this, he asked them who they were that they should pass judgment on his descent; upon which Quisquis struck him, and gave him chillca leaves instead of coca. When he was thus outraged, Huascar raised his eyes, and cried out: 'O Lord and Creator, how is it possible? Why hast thou sent me these burdens and troubles.' In those days Quisquis ordered all the children of Huascar Ynca to be slain, and all his servants, up to fifteen hundred persons, who were within the palace of Puca-marca.
summary.zh: 他們以繩套住印加王之頸以辱之;基斯-基斯喚他「科卡哈喬」與「蘇利亞」——意為私生子、嚼古柯者——並加以種種凌辱。二將又辱其母:「過來啊,瑪瑪·奧克略,你這瓦伊納·卡帕克的妾!」瓦伊斯卡爾聞言,反問對方何人,竟敢評斷他的血統;基斯-基斯當即掌摑之,並以奇爾卡葉充作古柯遞給他。受此奇恥,瓦伊斯卡爾舉目望天,呼曰:「主啊,造物主,怎麼可能如此?你為何將這些重負與苦難加於我身?」其後,基斯-基斯下令盡殺瓦伊斯卡爾諸子及其僕從——普卡-馬爾卡宮中的1500口皆死。

sensitivity.note: The humiliation cycle; the coca/chillca substitution is a specific ritual insult - coca is sacred, chillca is a weed.

title.en: The Cock Knew His Name: Spaniards Taken for Uiracocha
title.zh: 雞鳴知名:西班牙人被誤作維拉科查

region.zh: 卡哈馬卡與庫斯科(象徵性標記)

source.work: Juan de Santa Cruz Pachacuti-yamqui Salcamayhua, 'An Account of the Antiquities of Peru', in Narratives of the Rites and Laws of the Yncas, trans. C. R. Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1873

summary.en: In a few days the news arrived that the Spaniards had landed, and there was great dismay; by the advice of Quisquis great riches were buried in the earth, and Huascar had previously ordered a chain of gold and three thousand loads of gold and silver concealed in Cunti-suyu. Francisco Pizarro captured Atahuallpa in the midst of a vast concourse of Indians, after he had spoken with the friar Vicente de Valverde, when twelve thousand men were killed: for the people thought that they were the messengers of Pachayachachic Uiracocha, and when they fired off their guns, it was supposed to be Uiracocha. When Atahuallpa was in prison the cock crowed, and he said that even the birds knew his name; from that time they called the Spaniards Uiracocha, because they declared they brought the law of God, and the cock Atahuallpa. Atahuallpa sent messages to Antamarca with orders that Huascar should be killed, and began to pretend to be sad to deceive Pizarro; Huascar Ynca was killed in Antamarca with his son, wife and mother, with great cruelty. Atahuallpa was baptized and called Don Francisco, and afterwards he was put to death as a traitor.
summary.zh: 數日之後,西班牙人登陸的消息傳來,舉國震恐。依基斯-基斯之議,大批財寶被埋入土中;瓦伊斯卡爾此前已命將金鏈與三千馱金銀藏於昆蒂蘇尤。弗朗西斯科·皮薩羅在萬民簇擁中擒獲阿塔瓦爾帕——此前他剛與瓦爾韋爾德修士對話——一萬二千人被殺:因為人民以為他們是帕查亞查奇·維拉科查的信使;他們放槍時,眾人以為那便是維拉科查。阿塔瓦爾帕在獄中,雄雞啼鳴,他說:連鳥兒都知道我的名字。自那時起,人們稱西班牙人為「維拉科查」——因為他們自稱帶來上帝的律法——而稱雄雞為「阿塔瓦爾帕」。阿塔瓦爾帕遣使至安塔馬爾卡,下令處死瓦伊斯卡爾,隨即假裝悲慟以欺騙皮薩羅;瓦伊斯卡爾與其子、妻、母在安塔馬爾卡慘遭殺害。阿塔瓦爾帕受洗名「堂·弗朗西斯科」,後以叛國之罪被處死。

sensitivity.note: The conquest told through native eyes: the theophanic misrecognition of the invaders; the ethnonym 'Viracocha' for Spaniards originates here.

passages.text: But in a few days the news arrived that the Spaniards had landed, and there was great dismay. By the advice of Quisquis great riches were buried in the earth; and it is also said that Huascar had previously ordered a chain of gold and three thousand loads of gold, with as many of silver, to be concealed in Cunti-suyu.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Salcamayhua, Antiquities of Peru (Markham 1873); not verbatim.

passages.text: Francisco Pizarro captured Atahuallpa in the midst of a vast concourse of Indians, after he had spoken with the friar Vicente de Valverde, when twelve thousand men were killed. For the people thought that they were the messengers of Pachayachachic Uiracocha; and when they fired off their guns, it was supposed to be Uiracocha. When Atahuallpa was in prison the cock crowed, and he said that even the birds knew his name. From that time they called the Spaniards Uiracocha, because they declared to Atahuallpa that they brought the law of God. Hence they called the Spaniards Uiracocha, and the cock Atahuallpa.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Salcamayhua, Antiquities of Peru (Markham 1873); not verbatim.

passages.text: This Atahuallpa sent messages to Antamarca with orders that Huascar should be killed; and after he had sent them he began to pretend to be sad, trying to deceive the captain, Francisco Pizarro. So, by orders of Atahuallpa, they killed Huascar Ynca in Antamarca, with his son, wife, and mother, with great cruelty. Atahuallpa was baptized and called Don Francisco, and afterwards he was put to death as a traitor.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Salcamayhua, Antiquities of Peru (Markham 1873); not verbatim.
